Estimate monitored commercial catch

Source: R/run_catch.R
run_catch.Rd

Estimate monitored commercial catch

run_catch(sim)

Arguments

sim

A simulation returned by sim_fishery() or sim_fisheries().

Value

The simulation list with three keyed data tables in fishery$catch_estimates named total_catch, catch_at_length, and catch_at_age. Each has fishery, sim, year, and estimated numbers of fish n_hat. The composition tables also include length or age, mean_weight_kg (kilograms per fish), prop_mature (a proportion), and weight_status and maturity_status. A trait status is "estimated", inherits an unsupported composition status, or indicates "no_bin_sample", "no_weight_support", or "no_maturity_support". Means are missing for empty groups and when the corresponding trait is unsupported. A supported group of entirely immature fish has proportion zero. fishery$catch_diagnostics gives annual reported_n, operation counts (n_operations, n_positive_operations, n_sampled_operations), biological counts (n_measured, n_aged), the fraction of operations selected (operation_coverage), and the fraction of reported catch in selected operations (reported_catch_coverage). Fractions with zero denominators are missing. Both length_status and age_status can be "estimated", "zero_reported_catch", "no_operation_support", or "no_measurement_support". The age_status can also be "no_aging_support". Re-estimation clears previous catch comparisons and their error summaries.

Details

Total catch is the sum of reported numbers from all operations in each fishery, replicate, and year. For the length composition, each measured fish contributes its operation's reported catch divided by the operation inclusion probability and the number of measured fish in that operation. Length estimates use the population's native length groups.

For the age composition, each aged fish's weight also divides by its conditional aging probability. This supports random aging and aging by length group. Each composition is calibrated separately to the reported total. These estimates can differ from realized catch when reporting is biased. Only observed reports, inclusion probabilities, and biological samples are used.

A zero reported total gives zero estimates at every length and age. With positive reported catch, composition estimates require known positive inclusion probabilities for every operation reporting catch and measurements from every selected operation reporting catch. At least one measured fish must come from an operation with a positive report. Operations with positive inclusion probabilities can be unselected by chance. When measurement support is sufficient, missing observed ages, missing or invalid conditional aging probabilities, and absence of aged fish can leave age estimates unsupported while length estimates remain available. Unobserved lengths or ages within supported groups have estimated counts of zero.

Mean weight and mature proportion are weighted means of the observed values within each length or age group. Mean weight uses the length weights for measured fish and the age weights for aged fish. Maturity at length additionally accounts for the probability of maturity examination among measured fish. That probability is one with maturity_sampling = "measured" and the conditional aging probability with "aged". At age, the aging weight accounts for the joint observation of age and maturity under either protocol. Calibration to total catch cancels in each mean. Disabling maturity sampling leaves its means missing.

See also

catch_error()

Examples

# \donttest{
population <- sim_abundance(ages = 1:3, years = 2001:2002) |>
  sim_distribution(grid = make_grid(res = c(20, 20)))
result <- population |>
  sim_fisheries(trawl = sim_fishery(target = 0.1, catch_model = sim_capture(0.1),
                                    max_operations = 10)) |>
  run_catch() |>
  catch_error()
result$fishery$catch_estimates$catch_at_length
